expectations.text: Gives an explicit decision (apply, redirect, decline, ask, or equivalent) for every one of the 10 comments
expectations.evidence: Summary table: Take (C1, C2), 'Take, in plain words' (C3, C9), 'Decline for this PR' (C4), Decline (C5, C6, C8), Partial (C7), 'Keep the claim, name the mechanism' (C10).

expectations.text: Accepts C1 (missing empty_table import), C2 (prose says 'both return 6' but the table has no 6), and C3 (with_serial alone is insufficient when several columns share state); the C3 fix points readers to barriers or the concept guide
expectations.evidence: C1, C2 and C3 are taken. The C3 paragraph reads: 'marking each one with `with_serial` isn't enough — you also need [barriers](../../conceptual/query-engine/parallelization.md#barriers).'

expectations.text: Does not accept C4 as written: declines it or asks, citing that Crash Course page titles are title case by established convention (or an earlier reviewer decision)
expectations.evidence: 'Decline for this PR ... every Crash Course chapter title uses title case ... Changing only this chapter would make it the one odd entry in the Crash Course sidebar.'

expectations.text: For C5, C6 and C7, does not propose adding the property names, defaults or exact threshold values to the tutorial narrative (redirects to a Configuration section/reference link or declines, with reasons)
expectations.evidence: C5 and C6 are declined. C7 is Partial, and its proposed line-57 text says only 'a few million by default', with the reply saying it 'left out the property name and the Table/RowSet special case'.

expectations.text: Declines C8: does not propose enlarging the executed corrected example above the ~4.2M-row threshold (cites docs-build cost and/or that the page already explains the small size)
expectations.evidence: 'Decline. ... It would also make the snapshot test call a Python function more than 4 million times. ... The note at line 198 already tells readers the 100-row example wouldn't show the race.'

expectations.text: For C9, proposes a corrected takeaway at tutorial resolution (e.g. 'treats formulas as safe to run in parallel') rather than enumerating the conditions or naming properties
expectations.evidence: 'By default, Deephaven assumes your formulas are stateless and is free to run them in parallel ...' followed by 'Don't list the four conditions in a takeaway bullet.'

expectations.text: For C10, verifies the claim against source (e.g. the SelectColumn.isParallelizable javadoc: the engine may evaluate a non-parallelizable column out of order) and keeps the clause or asks, rather than deleting it or adding a hedge
expectations.evidence: 'the claim is supported. `SelectColumn.isParallelizable()` javadoc says: "Even if a column is not parallelizable, the engine may choose to evaluate it out-of-order ..."' It is kept and stated plainly in the rewrite.

expectations.text: Drafts a reply for every comment, and every reply for a comment that isn't applied gives a reason
expectations.evidence: Each of C1-C10 has a Reply. The declined replies for C4, C5, C6 and C8 give reasons (series convention, tutorial level, incomplete framing, free-threading and test cost).
